intent:
A live run of `action/agent.py` on main (2026-10-17) returned 20 `info`
"holds" findings and no drift, after reading only five files outside `.okf/`,
and citing lines in files it never opened. It never looked at `docs/` at all:
the default prompt runs kmctl's audit skill, which covers only `.okf/`
concepts that are due. That is not an audit.

This ticket makes it two audits, run separately, each comparing one folder
against the code:

- **Docs audit**, `new:action/prompts/docs-audit.md`: every page in `docs/`
  against the code it describes (commands and flags against the CLI's real
  `--help`, how-tos against `action.yml` and the workflows, file paths and
  defaults against the files).
- **Knowledge audit**, `new:action/prompts/okf-audit.md`: every concept in
  `.okf/` (decisions, architecture, practices; not handoffs) against the
  code its concrete claims name. It may load kmctl's audit skills, but it
  checks every concept, not only those due. It becomes `run`'s default
  prompt, so `run` keeps a shipped default.

Both prompts ship as files, so a user can copy and edit them. Changes to
`action/agent.py`:

- `Report` gains `checked`: one entry per page or concept compared, naming
  what it was compared against. `findings` holds mismatches only: each cites
  the claim (`path:line` in the audited folder) and the code that
  contradicts it, with a suggested fix. The prompts say no finding for
  something that holds.
- The script records every path the agent read or got search hits from. An
  output validator sends the agent back (PydanticAI `ModelRetry`) when any
  finding or `checked` entry cites a file it never opened, or a line past
  the file's end. Prompts may, code must.

  Measured on that live run's transcript: of 61 citations, 18 point at a
  file the agent never read and a line no search returned (strict variant:
  the file read, or that exact `path:line` a search hit). 10 of those 18
  name files it never touched at all (`src/kmctl/antigravity.py`,
  `review_due.py`, `scaffold.py`, `handoffs.py`, the release workflows).
  The check would have sent that run back on 18 of 61 citations, and the
  run's "holds" verdicts for ADRs 0006, 0012, 0015, 0016 and 0018 rest on
  them.

`.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` runs both: the audit and publish
jobs take a matrix of `docs` and `okf`, with artifacts `agent-report-docs`
and `agent-report-okf`, and issues titled "Docs audit" and "Knowledge
audit". `action.yml`, `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md`
and ADR 0017 (a correction) say the same.

Done when: the offline tests pass for the new report shape and the evidence
check, and a live run of each prompt on a copy of the repo with planted
false claims (at least three in `docs/`, three in `.okf/`) reports each
planted claim as a finding, recorded in a spike.

## Could invalidate this plan

- A Flash-class model may not catch planted drift with one run over a whole
  folder, even with the evidence check; then the plan needs per-page runs or
  a stronger default model instead of one prompt per folder. Spike: draft
  both prompts, plant false claims in a copy of the repo, run each live.
- The evidence check may send the agent into retry loops it cannot leave
  (search hits cite files it then must read, line numbers it guesses),
  burning the request cap. The same spike shows how often it retries.
